functions.name: s2n_connection_get_selected_cert
functions.signature: S2N_API extern struct s2n_cert_chain_and_key *s2n_connection_get_selected_cert(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Returns the certificate selected/used during the handshake (server’s chosen cert or client’s sent cert). Returns NULL if selection phase not complete or not requested.
requirements: conn must be valid

functions.name: s2n_cert_chain_get_length
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_cert_chain_get_length(const struct s2n_cert_chain_and_key *chain_and_key, uint32_t *cert_length);
functions.description: Returns the number of certificates in the certificate chain.
requirements: chain_and_key must be valid
cert_length must be a non-NULL output pointer

functions.name: s2n_cert_chain_get_cert
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_cert_chain_get_cert(const struct s2n_cert_chain_and_key *chain_and_key, struct s2n_cert **out_cert, const uint32_t cert_idx);
functions.description: Retrieves a pointer to the s2n_cert at index cert_idx in the chain (leaf index 0). out_cert is valid until chain_and_key is freed.
requirements: chain_and_key must be valid and not NULL
out_cert must be non-NULL output pointer
cert_idx must be within chain bounds

functions.name: s2n_cert_get_der
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_cert_get_der(const struct s2n_cert *cert, const uint8_t **out_cert_der, uint32_t *cert_length);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the DER encoding of the certificate and its length. Memory owned by s2n-tls and valid only while the connection exists.
requirements: cert must be valid
out_cert_der and cert_length must be non-NULL output pointers
Caller must copy if persistence beyond connection lifetime is needed

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_peer_cert_chain
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_connection_get_peer_cert_chain(const struct s2n_connection *conn, struct s2n_cert_chain_and_key *cert_chain);
functions.description: Returns the validated peer certificate chain into a caller-allocated empty s2n_cert_chain_and_key object.
requirements: conn must be valid
cert_chain must be allocated via s2n_cert_chain_and_key_new and be empty at call time
Caller frees cert_chain via s2n_cert_chain_and_key_free

functions.name: s2n_cert_get_x509_extension_value_length
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_cert_get_x509_extension_value_length(struct s2n_cert *cert, const uint8_t *oid, uint32_t *ext_value_len);
functions.description: Returns the DER-encoded extension value length for the X.509 extension identified by OID string.
requirements: cert must be valid
oid must be a NULL-terminated cstring OID
ext_value_len must be a non-NULL output pointer

functions.name: s2n_cert_get_x509_extension_value
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_cert_get_x509_extension_value(struct s2n_cert *cert, const uint8_t *oid, uint8_t *ext_value, uint32_t *ext_value_len, bool *critical);
functions.description: Returns the DER-encoded extension value for a given extension OID into ext_value, setting its actual length and critical flag. ext_value_len is in/out for buffer sizing.
requirements: cert must be valid
oid must be a NULL-terminated cstring OID
ext_value must be a buffer of at least *ext_value_len on input
ext_value_len and critical must be non-NULL pointers

functions.name: s2n_cert_get_utf8_string_from_extension_data_length
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_cert_get_utf8_string_from_extension_data_length(const uint8_t *extension_data, uint32_t extension_len, uint32_t *utf8_str_len);
functions.description: Returns the UTF-8 string length after decoding the provided DER-encoded extension value.
requirements: extension_data must point to extension_len bytes
utf8_str_len must be a non-NULL output pointer

functions.name: s2n_cert_get_utf8_string_from_extension_data
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_cert_get_utf8_string_from_extension_data(const uint8_t *extension_data, uint32_t extension_len, uint8_t *out_data, uint32_t *out_len);
functions.description: Decodes DER-encoded extension data into a UTF-8 string written to out_data. out_len is in/out for buffer sizing and actual length.
requirements: extension_data must point to extension_len bytes
out_data must be a buffer of at least *out_len on input
out_len must be a non-NULL pointer

functions.name: s2n_external_psk_new
functions.signature: S2N_API struct s2n_psk *s2n_external_psk_new(void);
functions.description: Creates a new external PSK object with default hash algorithm S2N_PSK_HMAC_SHA256.
requirements: Caller must free with s2n_psk_free

functions.name: s2n_psk_free
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_psk_free(struct s2n_psk **psk);
functions.description: Frees an s2n_psk and clears its memory.
requirements: psk must be a non-NULL pointer to a pointer to an s2n_psk created by s2n_external_psk_new

functions.name: s2n_psk_set_identity
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_psk_set_identity(struct s2n_psk *psk, const uint8_t *identity, uint16_t identity_size);
functions.description: Sets the external PSK identity (non-secret raw bytes). Identity is copied.
requirements: psk must be valid
identity must point to identity_size bytes
Identity SHOULD NOT contain sensitive data (transmitted in clear)

functions.name: s2n_psk_set_secret
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_psk_set_secret(struct s2n_psk *psk, const uint8_t *secret, uint16_t secret_size);
functions.description: Sets the externally provisioned PSK secret. Secret is copied.
requirements: psk must be valid
secret must point to secret_size bytes
Do not derive secrets from low-entropy inputs (dictionary attack risk)

functions.name: s2n_psk_set_hmac
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_psk_set_hmac(struct s2n_psk *psk, s2n_psk_hmac hmac);
functions.description: Sets the hash algorithm for the PSK.
requirements: psk must be valid
hmac must be a valid s2n_psk_hmac value

functions.name: s2n_connection_append_psk
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_connection_append_psk(struct s2n_connection *conn, struct s2n_psk *psk);
functions.description: Appends a PSK to the connection’s list. Fails if a duplicate identity exists. The connection stores a copy; caller still owns and must free the original PSK.
requirements: conn must be valid
psk must be a valid PSK with identity/secret configured appropriately

functions.name: s2n_config_set_psk_mode
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_config_set_psk_mode(struct s2n_config *config, s2n_psk_mode mode);
functions.description: Sets the PSK mode (resumption or external) on the config.
requirements: config must be valid
mode must be S2N_PSK_MODE_RESUMPTION or S2N_PSK_MODE_EXTERNAL

functions.name: s2n_connection_set_psk_mode
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_connection_set_psk_mode(struct s2n_connection *conn, s2n_psk_mode mode);
functions.description: Sets the PSK mode on the connection, overriding the config.
requirements: conn must be valid
mode must be S2N_PSK_MODE_RESUMPTION or S2N_PSK_MODE_EXTERNAL

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_negotiated_psk_identity_length
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_connection_get_negotiated_psk_identity_length(struct s2n_connection *conn, uint16_t *identity_length);
functions.description: Gets the length of the negotiated PSK identity. Returns 0 if no PSK was negotiated.
requirements: conn must be valid
identity_length must be a non-NULL output pointer

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_negotiated_psk_identity
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_connection_get_negotiated_psk_identity(struct s2n_connection *conn, uint8_t *identity, uint16_t max_identity_length);
functions.description: Copies the negotiated PSK identity into identity if present. Caller should check non-zero length via s2n_connection_get_negotiated_psk_identity_length first.
requirements: conn must be valid
identity must be a buffer of size >= max_identity_length

functions.name: s2n_offered_psk_new
functions.signature: S2N_API struct s2n_offered_psk *s2n_offered_psk_new(void);
functions.description: Allocates a new offered PSK object for server-side PSK selection workflows.
requirements: Caller must free with s2n_offered_psk_free

functions.name: s2n_offered_psk_free
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_offered_psk_free(struct s2n_offered_psk **psk);
functions.description: Frees an offered PSK object.
requirements: psk must be a non-NULL pointer to pointer allocated via s2n_offered_psk_new

functions.name: s2n_offered_psk_get_identity
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_offered_psk_get_identity(struct s2n_offered_psk *psk, uint8_t **identity, uint16_t *size);
functions.description: Gets the identity and size for an offered PSK.
requirements: psk must be valid
identity and size must be non-NULL output pointers

functions.name: s2n_offered_psk_list_has_next
functions.signature: S2N_API bool s2n_offered_psk_list_has_next(struct s2n_offered_psk_list *psk_list);
functions.description: Checks if there is another PSK in the offered PSK list. Returned pointer usage is limited to the callback scope.
requirements: psk_list must be valid
Pointer/lifetime note: the list reference is invalid after s2n_psk_selection_callback returns

functions.name: s2n_offered_psk_list_next
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_offered_psk_list_next(struct s2n_offered_psk_list *psk_list, struct s2n_offered_psk *psk);
functions.description: Retrieves the next offered PSK in the list into the provided psk object. Use has_next first to check availability.
requirements: psk_list must be valid
psk must be a valid offered PSK object to receive data

functions.name: s2n_offered_psk_list_reread
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_offered_psk_list_reread(struct s2n_offered_psk_list *psk_list);
functions.description: Resets the offered PSK list read cursor back to the start.
requirements: psk_list must be valid

functions.name: s2n_offered_psk_list_choose_psk
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_offered_psk_list_choose_psk(struct s2n_offered_psk_list *psk_list, struct s2n_offered_psk *psk);
functions.description: Chooses a PSK for the connection by matching the offered identity against the server’s known PSKs. Errors if no match.
requirements: psk_list must be valid
psk must be a valid offered PSK obtained from the list

functions.name: s2n_config_set_psk_selection_callback
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_config_set_psk_selection_callback(struct s2n_config *config, s2n_psk_selection_callback cb, void *context);
functions.description: Registers a server-side callback to select the matching PSK from the offered list. If unset, default logic selects first matching server PSK.
requirements: config must be valid
cb must follow s2n_psk_selection_callback semantics
context pointer must remain valid during callback use

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_wire_bytes_in
functions.signature: S2N_API extern uint64_t s2n_connection_get_wire_bytes_in(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes received on the wire for the connection.
requirements: conn must be valid

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_wire_bytes_out
functions.signature: S2N_API extern uint64_t s2n_connection_get_wire_bytes_out(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes transmitted on the wire for the connection.
requirements: conn must be valid

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_client_protocol_version
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_connection_get_client_protocol_version(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Returns the highest protocol version supported by the client, using predefined S2N_* constants.
requirements: conn must be valid

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_server_protocol_version
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_connection_get_server_protocol_version(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Returns the highest protocol version supported by the server, using predefined S2N_* constants.
requirements: conn must be valid

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_actual_protocol_version
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_connection_get_actual_protocol_version(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Returns the protocol version actually negotiated for the connection, using predefined S2N_* constants.
requirements: conn must be valid

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_client_hello_version
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_connection_get_client_hello_version(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Returns the protocol version used in the initial ClientHello message for this connection, using predefined S2N_* constants.
requirements: conn must be valid

functions.name: s2n_client_hello_get_legacy_record_version
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_client_hello_get_legacy_record_version(struct s2n_client_hello *ch, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Returns the record-layer version in the first record containing the ClientHello. Deprecated and only useful for logging/fingerprinting.
requirements: ch must be valid
out must be a non-NULL output pointer

functions.name: s2n_connection_client_cert_used
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_connection_client_cert_used(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Returns 1 if Client Auth was negotiated and used on the connection, else 0.
requirements: conn must be valid

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_cipher
functions.signature: S2N_API extern const char *s2n_connection_get_cipher(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Returns the OpenSSL-style human-readable ciphersuite name negotiated, or a placeholder before handshake completes.
requirements: conn must be valid
Accurate only after handshake

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_certificate_match
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_connection_get_certificate_match(struct s2n_connection *conn, s2n_cert_sni_match *match_status);
functions.description: Reports whether and how the server matched the client’s SNI to a certificate (none/exact/wildcard/no match).
requirements: conn must be valid
match_status must be a non-NULL output pointer
Valid after certificate selection phase

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_master_secret
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_connection_get_master_secret(const struct s2n_connection *conn, uint8_t *secret_bytes, size_t max_size);
functions.description: Copies the pre-TLS1.3 48-byte master secret into secret_bytes. Dangerous; not supported for TLS1.3 and may fail. Prefer exporters.
requirements: conn must be valid and negotiated in a version that supports master secret access (not TLS1.3)
secret_bytes must be a buffer with max_size >= 48

functions.name: s2n_connection_tls_exporter
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_connection_tls_exporter(struct s2n_connection *conn, const uint8_t *label, uint32_t label_length, const uint8_t *context, uint32_t context_length, uint8_t *output, uint32_t output_length);
functions.description: Implements TLS exporter API to derive keying material from a TLS1.3 connection after handshake. Writes output_length bytes to output based on label and optional context.
requirements: conn must be valid and handshake completed
label must point to label_length bytes
context may be NULL or point to context_length bytes
output must be a buffer of size >= output_length

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_cipher_iana_value
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_connection_get_cipher_iana_value(struct s2n_connection *conn, uint8_t *first, uint8_t *second);
functions.description: Returns the two-byte IANA value of the negotiated ciphersuite into first and second. Only after negotiation.
requirements: conn must be valid
first and second must be non-NULL output pointers
Handshake must have negotiated a ciphersuite

functions.name: s2n_connection_is_valid_for_cipher_preferences
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_connection_is_valid_for_cipher_preferences(struct s2n_connection *conn, const char *version);
functions.description: Checks if the connection’s negotiated parameters satisfy the given security policy. Returns 1 if valid, 0 if not, -1 on error.
requirements: conn must be valid
version must be a valid policy string

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_curve
functions.signature: S2N_API extern const char *s2n_connection_get_curve(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Deprecated. Returns the human-readable ECDHE curve name used, or "NONE" if none.
requirements: conn must be valid

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_kem_name
functions.signature: S2N_API extern const char *s2n_connection_get_kem_name(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Deprecated. Returns the human-readable PQ KEM name for TLS1.2 PQ experiments, or "NONE" if none.
requirements: conn must be valid

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_kem_group_name
functions.signature: S2N_API extern const char *s2n_connection_get_kem_group_name(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Returns the human-readable KEM group name (TLS1.3 PQ key exchange) or "NONE" if no PQ exchange occurred.
requirements: conn must be valid

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_key_exchange_group
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_connection_get_key_exchange_group(struct s2n_connection *conn, const char **group_name);
functions.description: Returns the human-readable key exchange group name (EC group or hybrid PQ group). Fails if neither ECDHE nor PQ group negotiated.
requirements: conn must be valid
group_name must be a non-NULL output pointer

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_alert
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_connection_get_alert(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Returns the TLS alert code that caused the connection to close, if any.
requirements: conn must be valid

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_handshake_type_name
functions.signature: S2N_API extern const char *s2n_connection_get_handshake_type_name(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description of the handshake type processed, e.g., "NEGOTIATED|FULL_HANDSHAKE|PERFECT_FORWARD_SECRECY".
requirements: conn must be valid

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_last_message_name
functions.signature: S2N_API extern const char *s2n_connection_get_last_message_name(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Returns the human-readable name of the last TLS message processed.
requirements: conn must be valid

functions.name: s2n_config_set_async_pkey_callback
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_config_set_async_pkey_callback(struct s2n_config *config, s2n_async_pkey_fn fn);
functions.description: Registers a callback to handle private key operations (sign/decrypt) asynchronously during handshake.
requirements: config must be valid
fn must follow s2n_async_pkey_fn semantics (op must be freed by application)

functions.name: s2n_async_pkey_op_perform
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_async_pkey_op_perform(struct s2n_async_pkey_op *op, s2n_cert_private_key *key);
functions.description: Performs the pending private key operation using the provided private key. Can be called once; safe in callback or another thread if op not shared concurrently.
requirements: op must be valid and not yet performed
key must be a valid private key corresponding to the operation
Can be called from inside callback or another thread (no concurrent access to op)

functions.name: s2n_async_pkey_op_apply
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_async_pkey_op_apply(struct s2n_async_pkey_op *op, struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Finalizes the async private key operation and unblocks the connection. Can be called once; must be after perform.
requirements: op must be valid and performed
conn must be the same connection that triggered the operation
Can be called from inside callback or another thread (no concurrent access to op)

functions.name: s2n_async_pkey_op_free
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_async_pkey_op_free(struct s2n_async_pkey_op *op);
functions.description: Frees the async private key operation. Must be called for every operation passed to the callback.
requirements: op must be a valid operation handle (can be freed before or after connection freed)

functions.name: s2n_config_set_async_pkey_validation_mode
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_config_set_async_pkey_validation_mode(struct s2n_config *config, s2n_async_pkey_validation_mode mode);
functions.description: Configures validation strictness for results of async private key operations on connections using this config.
requirements: config must be valid
mode must be a valid s2n_async_pkey_validation_mode value

functions.name: s2n_async_pkey_op_get_op_type
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_async_pkey_op_get_op_type(struct s2n_async_pkey_op *op, s2n_async_pkey_op_type *type);
functions.description: Returns the type (decrypt or sign) of the pending private key operation.
requirements: op must be valid
type must be a non-NULL output pointer

functions.name: s2n_async_pkey_op_get_input_size
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_async_pkey_op_get_input_size(struct s2n_async_pkey_op *op, uint32_t *data_len);
functions.description: Returns the size of input data required for the private key operation.
requirements: op must be valid
data_len must be a non-NULL output pointer

functions.name: s2n_async_pkey_op_get_input
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_async_pkey_op_get_input(struct s2n_async_pkey_op *op, uint8_t *data, uint32_t data_len);
functions.description: Copies the input to the private key operation into data buffer (digest for sign or ciphertext for decrypt; ML-DSA uses external mu pre-hash).
requirements: op must be valid
data must be a buffer with size >= data_len and at least the required input size
Use s2n_async_pkey_op_get_input_size to size buffer

functions.name: s2n_async_pkey_op_set_output
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_async_pkey_op_set_output(struct s2n_async_pkey_op *op, const uint8_t *data, uint32_t data_len);
functions.description: Sets the output of the private key operation (signature or decrypted data). s2n-tls does not take ownership of the buffer.
requirements: op must be valid
data must point to data_len bytes representing the operation’s output

functions.name: s2n_config_set_key_log_cb
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_config_set_key_log_cb(struct s2n_config *config, s2n_key_log_fn callback, void *ctx);
functions.description: Sets a key logging callback that emits secrets in NSS Key Log format for debugging. Dangerous; for debugging only.
requirements: config must be valid
callback must follow s2n_key_log_fn; logline must be consumed before return
ctx must remain valid for as long as callback is set

functions.name: s2n_config_enable_cert_req_dss_legacy_compat
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_config_enable_cert_req_dss_legacy_compat(struct s2n_config *config);
functions.description: Enables sending DSS cert type in CertificateRequest for legacy compatibility only; handshake will not succeed if a DSS cert is actually received.
requirements: config must be valid
Only call if legacy DSS certificate type compatibility is truly required

functions.name: s2n_config_set_server_max_early_data_size
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_config_set_server_max_early_data_size(struct s2n_config *config, uint32_t max_early_data_size);
functions.description: Configures the server-wide maximum number of early data bytes accepted. Default 0 (reject all).
requirements: config must be valid

functions.name: s2n_connection_set_server_max_early_data_size
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_connection_set_server_max_early_data_size(struct s2n_connection *conn, uint32_t max_early_data_size);
functions.description: Overrides the server maximum early data size for a specific connection.
requirements: conn must be valid

functions.name: s2n_connection_set_server_early_data_context
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_connection_set_server_early_data_context(struct s2n_connection *conn, const uint8_t *context, uint16_t context_size);
functions.description: Sets a byte-buffer context used during early data acceptance decisions for session resumption. Data is copied and serialized into tickets.
requirements: conn must be valid
context must point to context_size bytes

functions.name: s2n_psk_configure_early_data
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_psk_configure_early_data(struct s2n_psk *psk, uint32_t max_early_data_size, uint8_t cipher_suite_first_byte, uint8_t cipher_suite_second_byte);
functions.description: Configures an external PSK to allow early data, setting its maximum size and associated ciphersuite IANA value. Ciphersuite’s HMAC must match PSK HMAC.
requirements: psk must be valid (created via s2n_external_psk_new)
max_early_data_size must reflect server policy
Associated ciphersuite must match PSK’s HMAC and the negotiated ciphersuite

functions.name: s2n_psk_set_application_protocol
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_psk_set_application_protocol(struct s2n_psk *psk, const uint8_t *application_protocol, uint8_t size);
functions.description: Sets an optional ALPN application protocol for the PSK. Must match the negotiated ALPN when using early data.
requirements: psk must be valid
application_protocol must point to size bytes (copied)

functions.name: s2n_psk_set_early_data_context
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_psk_set_early_data_context(struct s2n_psk *psk, const uint8_t *context, uint16_t size);
functions.description: Sets an optional user early data context on the PSK for use by early data callback logic. Context data is copied.
requirements: psk must be valid
context must point to size bytes

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_early_data_status
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_connection_get_early_data_status(struct s2n_connection *conn, s2n_early_data_status_t *status);
functions.description: Reports the current early data status for the connection (OK, NOT_REQUESTED, REJECTED, END).
requirements: conn must be valid
status must be a non-NULL output pointer

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_remaining_early_data_size
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_connection_get_remaining_early_data_size(struct s2n_connection *conn, uint32_t *allowed_early_data_size);
functions.description: Reports remaining early data that can still be sent/received for the connection given current status and limits.
requirements: conn must be valid
allowed_early_data_size must be a non-NULL output pointer

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_max_early_data_size
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_connection_get_max_early_data_size(struct s2n_connection *conn, uint32_t *max_early_data_size);
functions.description: Reports the maximum early data size allowed by the connection, independent of current status.
requirements: conn must be valid
max_early_data_size must be a non-NULL output pointer

functions.name: s2n_send_early_data
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_send_early_data(struct s2n_connection *conn, const uint8_t *data, ssize_t data_len, ssize_t *data_sent, s2n_blocked_status *blocked);
functions.description: Client API to begin negotiation and attempt to send early data. Returns bytes sent and blocked status like s2n_negotiate. Use only with proper anti-replay mitigations.
requirements: conn must be valid and configured for early data
data must point to data_len bytes
data_sent and blocked must be non-NULL output pointers
Caller must handle partial sends and blocking semantics

functions.name: s2n_recv_early_data
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_recv_early_data(struct s2n_connection *conn, uint8_t *data, ssize_t max_data_len, ssize_t *data_received, s2n_blocked_status *blocked);
functions.description: Server API to begin negotiation and accept any early data. Returns bytes received and blocked status like s2n_negotiate.
requirements: conn must be valid and configured for early data
data must be a buffer of size >= max_data_len
data_received and blocked must be non-NULL output pointers

functions.name: s2n_config_set_early_data_cb
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_config_set_early_data_cb(struct s2n_config *config, s2n_early_data_cb cb);
functions.description: Registers a server callback to accept or reject early data after standard TLS checks pass. Can be synchronous or asynchronous.
requirements: config must be valid
cb must follow s2n_early_data_cb semantics (must accept/reject or block by returning success without calling accept/reject)

functions.name: s2n_offered_early_data_get_context_length
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_offered_early_data_get_context_length(struct s2n_offered_early_data *early_data, uint16_t *context_len);
functions.description: Returns the length of the user-defined early data context associated with the offered early data.
requirements: early_data must be valid
context_len must be a non-NULL output pointer

functions.name: s2n_offered_early_data_get_context
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_offered_early_data_get_context(struct s2n_offered_early_data *early_data, uint8_t *context, uint16_t max_len);
functions.description: Copies the user-defined early data context into the provided buffer. Buffer must be sized using the length getter.
requirements: early_data must be valid
context must be a buffer of size >= max_len
Call context length getter to size buffer

functions.name: s2n_offered_early_data_reject
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_offered_early_data_reject(struct s2n_offered_early_data *early_data);
functions.description: Rejects the client’s offered early data in the early data callback context.
requirements: early_data must be valid

functions.name: s2n_offered_early_data_accept
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_offered_early_data_accept(struct s2n_offered_early_data *early_data);
functions.description: Accepts the client’s offered early data in the early data callback context.
requirements: early_data must be valid

functions.name: s2n_config_get_supported_groups
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_config_get_supported_groups(struct s2n_config *config, uint16_t *groups, uint16_t groups_count_max, uint16_t *groups_count);
functions.description: Retrieves the set of supported groups (IANA ids) from the config’s security policy and linked capabilities into groups; sets groups_count. Errors if capacity too small.
requirements: config must be valid
groups must be a buffer with capacity for groups_count_max entries
groups_count_max must be sufficient to hold all supported groups
groups_count must be a non-NULL output pointer

functions.name: s2n_config_set_serialization_version
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_config_set_serialization_version(struct s2n_config *config, s2n_serialization_version version);
functions.description: Sets the connection serialization feature version to use for connections created with this config. Required prior to handshake for serialization support.
requirements: config must be valid
version must be a valid s2n_serialization_version value

functions.name: s2n_connection_serialization_length
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_connection_serialization_length(struct s2n_connection *conn, uint32_t *length);
functions.description: Returns the buffer size required to serialize the given established connection. Size depends on negotiated parameters.
requirements: conn must be valid and handshake complete
length must be a non-NULL output pointer

functions.name: s2n_connection_serialize
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_connection_serialize(struct s2n_connection *conn, uint8_t *buffer, uint32_t buffer_length);
functions.description: Serializes an established connection into buffer for transfer/deserialization. Dangerous: exposes plaintext cryptographic material; must be encrypted and MACed off-box.
requirements: conn must be valid and handshake complete
Associated config must have serialization version set prior to handshake
No application data may remain in IO buffers (drain send/recv before serializing)
buffer must be at least the size returned by s2n_connection_serialization_length
Serialization unsupported for SSLv3

functions.name: s2n_connection_deserialize
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_connection_deserialize(struct s2n_connection *conn, uint8_t *buffer, uint32_t buffer_length);
functions.description: Deserializes a serialized connection into a fresh s2n_connection. Integrity of buffer is not verified; must be MACed and encrypted by the application.
requirements: conn must be a new s2n_connection
buffer must point to the serialized data of size buffer_length
Application must re-apply any desired config/connection settings post-deserialization

functions.name: s2n_config_set_cert_authorities_from_trust_store
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_config_set_cert_authorities_from_trust_store(struct s2n_config *config);
functions.description: Loads certificate authorities from the config’s trust store to advertise during handshake for client auth. Requires a trust store without default system certs and total size <= 10kB.
requirements: config must be valid
Trust store must not include default system certificates (use s2n_config_new_minimal or wipe trust store)
Total CAs size must not exceed ~10kB limit

functions.name: s2n_config_set_async_offload_callback
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_config_set_async_offload_callback(struct s2n_config *config, uint32_t allow_list, s2n_async_offload_cb fn, void *ctx);
functions.description: Registers an application-provided async offloading callback and specifies which handshake operations may be offloaded via an allow-list bitmask. Use this to move CPU-heavy handshake work (for allowed operations) out of the main event loop. If S2N_ASYNC_OFFLOAD_ALLOW_ALL is used, ensure the callback can handle any current or future offload type. The ctx pointer is stored and passed to the callback on each invocation. To actually offload work asynchronously, the callback should return success and perform the work via s2n_async_offload_op_perform() outside the callback; calling perform inside the callback is effectively synchronous.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized s2n_config pointer.
allow_list must be the bitwise-OR of s2n_async_offload_op_type values that the application is prepared to handle.
If using S2N_ASYNC_OFFLOAD_ALLOW_ALL, the callback must be able to support all supported and future offload operation types.
fn is the callback that will be invoked for each allowed operation encountered during the handshake; it must follow the s2n_async_offload_cb signature.
ctx is optional application data and may be NULL.
To offload work asynchronously: (1) the operation’s type must be included in allow_list; (2) the callback must return success and s2n_async_offload_op_perform() must be called outside the callback.

functions.name: s2n_async_offload_op_perform
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_async_offload_op_perform(struct s2n_async_offload_op *op);
functions.description: Executes the specific offloadable handshake operation represented by op. Call this from a worker thread to complete an operation that was deferred by the async offloading callback. Until this completes, s2n_negotiate() will return S2N_ERR_T_BLOCKED. Invoking this function from inside the callback performs the work synchronously.
requirements: op must be the opaque operation object provided by s2n-tls to the async offloading callback; it is owned by s2n-tls and eventually freed with the s2n_connection.
Each op may be passed to s2n_async_offload_op_perform() at most once.
To achieve asynchronous behavior, invoke s2n_async_offload_op_perform() outside of the callback (e.g., from a separate thread) and return success from the callback immediately.
While op is pending, repeated calls to s2n_negotiate() will return S2N_ERR_T_BLOCKED until s2n_async_offload_op_perform() completes.

functions.name: s2n_certificate_request_get_ca_list
functions.signature: struct s2n_certificate_authority_list *s2n_certificate_request_get_ca_list(struct s2n_certificate_request *request);
functions.description: Returns the certificate_authorities list advertised in the peer’s CertificateRequest. The returned pointer is borrowed (not a copy) and has the same lifetime as the s2n_certificate_request. It may be NULL if no list was provided. Typical usage is within a CertificateRequest callback to inspect acceptable issuer DNs before selecting a client certificate.
requirements: request must point to a valid s2n_certificate_request (typically only valid during the CertificateRequest callback).
The returned s2n_certificate_authority_list pointer, if non-NULL, is owned by s2n-tls; callers must not free or mutate its storage.
Callers must check for a NULL return (no list available).

functions.name: s2n_certificate_request_set_certificate
functions.signature: int s2n_certificate_request_set_certificate(struct s2n_certificate_request *request, struct s2n_cert_chain_and_key *chain);
functions.description: Associates the certificate chain/key to present in response to the CertificateRequest. Intended to be called from the CertificateRequest callback after examining request metadata (e.g., certificate_authorities). The chain must outlive the connection.
requirements: request must point to a valid s2n_certificate_request (typically within the CertificateRequest callback).
chain must be a valid, initialized s2n_cert_chain_and_key and must outlive the associated connection.
Do not free or modify chain for the duration of the connection (the implementation warns against freeing/modifying).
Return value must be checked: S2N_SUCCESS (0) on success, S2N_FAILURE (-1) on failure; on failure, s2n_errno should be consulted by the caller (standard s2n-tls error handling).

functions.name: s2n_certificate_authority_list_has_next
functions.signature: bool s2n_certificate_authority_list_has_next(struct s2n_certificate_authority_list *list);
functions.description: Indicates whether another certificate authority entry is available when iterating the offered certificate_authorities list. Used to drive iteration before calling ..._next to fetch entries.
requirements: list must be a valid s2n_certificate_authority_list obtained from s2n_certificate_request_get_ca_list.
Callers should use the boolean result to determine whether calling s2n_certificate_authority_list_next is valid.

functions.name: s2n_certificate_authority_list_next
functions.signature: int s2n_certificate_authority_list_next(struct s2n_certificate_authority_list *list, uint8_t **name, uint16_t *length);
functions.description: Retrieves the next certificate authority name from the list and returns its bytes and length. The name is the raw bytes sent by the server (commonly a DER-encoded DistinguishedName). The name pointer’s lifetime is tied to the list/request and must not outlive the callback scope.
requirements: list must be a valid s2n_certificate_authority_list obtained from s2n_certificate_request_get_ca_list.
name must be a non-NULL out-parameter to receive the pointer to the next name.
length must be a non-NULL out-parameter to receive the name length.
Should only be called when s2n_certificate_authority_list_has_next(list) returns true; otherwise it may fail.
The returned name pointer must not be freed or modified by the caller and must not be used after the list/request’s lifetime ends (e.g., after the callback).
Return value must be checked: S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure.

functions.name: s2n_certificate_authority_list_reread
functions.signature: int s2n_certificate_authority_list_reread(struct s2n_certificate_authority_list *list);
functions.description: Resets iteration over the certificate_authorities list to the beginning so entries can be read again from the start.
requirements: list must be a valid s2n_certificate_authority_list obtained from s2n_certificate_request_get_ca_list.
Return value must be checked: S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure.

functions.name: s2n_config_set_cert_request_callback
functions.signature: int s2n_config_set_cert_request_callback(struct s2n_config *config, s2n_cert_request_callback cert_req_callback, void *ctx);
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked after a CertificateRequest message is parsed (currently only on the client side). The callback receives the connection, user context, and the request object used to inspect CA list and set the certificate to send.
requirements: config must point to a valid, initialized s2n_config.
cert_req_callback must be a function matching the s2n_cert_request_callback signature; it will be invoked with (s2n_connection*, void*, s2n_certificate_request*).
ctx is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback; it need only be valid at callback invocation times.
Return value must be checked: S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure.

functions.name: s2n_cleanup_thread
functions.signature: S2N_API extern int s2n_cleanup_thread(void);
functions.description: Cleans up any internal thread-local resources used by s2n-tls for the calling thread. Typically invoked indirectly by s2n_cleanup, but may be called directly depending on your thread management model. Use this at thread teardown when a thread that used s2n-tls is exiting, especially if global s2n_cleanup is not appropriate or is deferred.
requirements: Call from the thread whose s2n-tls thread-local resources should be cleaned up (thread-local cleanup).
If you rely on s2n_cleanup to perform global cleanup, be aware it already calls this function; avoid redundant calls unless your thread model requires it.
Check the return value: returns S2N_SUCCESS on success and S2N_FAILURE on failure; handle failure accordingly.

functions.name: s2n_config_set_crl_lookup_cb
functions.signature: int s2n_config_set_crl_lookup_cb(struct s2n_config *config, s2n_crl_lookup_callback callback, void *context)
functions.description: Registers a callback to supply Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs) for CRL validation during the TLS handshake. The callback is invoked once per received certificate and may operate synchronously by calling s2n_crl_lookup_set/s2n_crl_lookup_ignore within the callback, or asynchronously by returning success and calling one of those later to unblock negotiation.
requirements: config must point to a valid s2n_config.
callback is invoked once per received certificate during handshake.
For synchronous use, the callback should call s2n_crl_lookup_set() or s2n_crl_lookup_ignore() before returning.

For asynchronous use, the callback may return success without calling the above; in that case, s2n_negotiate() will block with S2N_BLOCKED_ON_APPLICATION_INPUT until one of them is called for each invoked callback.
context is an application-provided pointer passed through unmodified to the callback.

functions.name: s2n_crl_new
functions.signature: struct s2n_crl *s2n_crl_new(void)
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new s2n_crl object to hold a CRL. Load PEM-encoded CRL data into it with s2n_crl_load_pem(), and free it with s2n_crl_free().
requirements: Returned s2n_crl* must be freed with s2n_crl_free().

functions.name: s2n_crl_load_pem
functions.signature: int s2n_crl_load_pem(struct s2n_crl *crl, uint8_t *pem, size_t len)
functions.description: Loads PEM-encoded CRL data into an existing s2n_crl object.
requirements: crl must be a valid s2n_crl allocated by s2n_crl_new().
pem must point to PEM-formatted CRL data; len must be the number of bytes available at pem.
pem must be at least len bytes accessible.
Function returns S2N_SUCCESS on success and S2N_FAILURE on error.

functions.name: s2n_crl_free
functions.signature: int s2n_crl_free(struct s2n_crl **crl)
functions.description: Frees an allocated s2n_crl and sets the caller’s pointer to NULL.
requirements: crl must be a non-NULL pointer to an s2n_crl* previously returned by s2n_crl_new().
May only be called to free objects allocated by s2n_crl_new().
On success, *crl is set to NULL.

functions.name: s2n_crl_get_issuer_hash
functions.signature: int s2n_crl_get_issuer_hash(struct s2n_crl *crl, uint64_t *hash)
functions.description: Retrieves the issuer hash associated with the CRL, which corresponds to the issuer hash of certificates provided to the CRL lookup callback via s2n_crl_lookup_get_cert_issuer_hash().
requirements: crl must be a valid, loaded s2n_crl.
hash must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the issuer hash value.
Returns S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure.

functions.name: s2n_crl_validate_active
functions.signature: int s2n_crl_validate_active(struct s2n_crl *crl)
functions.description: Checks whether the CRL is currently active based on its thisUpdate field compared to the current time. Returns success if active.
requirements: crl must be a valid s2n_crl containing a parsed CRL.
Returns S2N_SUCCESS if active; S2N_FAILURE if not active or status cannot be determined.

functions.name: s2n_crl_validate_not_expired
functions.signature: int s2n_crl_validate_not_expired(struct s2n_crl *crl)
functions.description: Checks whether the CRL has not expired based on its nextUpdate field relative to the current time. If nextUpdate is absent, the CRL is assumed to never expire. Returns success if not expired.
requirements: crl must be a valid s2n_crl containing a parsed CRL.
Returns S2N_SUCCESS if not expired; S2N_FAILURE if expired or expiration status cannot be determined.

functions.name: s2n_crl_lookup_get_cert_issuer_hash
functions.signature: int s2n_crl_lookup_get_cert_issuer_hash(struct s2n_crl_lookup *lookup, uint64_t *hash)
functions.description: From within a CRL lookup callback, obtains the issuer hash of the certificate currently being processed. This value can be matched to a CRL’s issuer hash via s2n_crl_get_issuer_hash().
requirements: lookup must be the lookup object provided to the CRL lookup callback.
hash must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the issuer hash.
Returns S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure.

functions.name: s2n_crl_lookup_set
functions.signature: int s2n_crl_lookup_set(struct s2n_crl_lookup *lookup, struct s2n_crl *crl)
functions.description: From within a CRL lookup callback, supplies a CRL to use when validating the certificate chain for the certificate associated with the lookup.
requirements: lookup must be the lookup object provided to the CRL lookup callback invocation.
crl must be a valid s2n_crl to include in validation for the associated certificate.
Intended to be called from within the CRL lookup callback; for asynchronous flows, it may be called after the callback returns to unblock s2n_negotiate().
Returns S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure.

functions.name: s2n_crl_lookup_ignore
functions.signature: int s2n_crl_lookup_ignore(struct s2n_crl_lookup *lookup)
functions.description: From within a CRL lookup callback, indicates that no CRL will be provided for the certificate associated with the lookup. If that certificate ends up in the chain of trust, validation will fail with S2N_ERR_CRL_LOOKUP_FAILED; otherwise validation proceeds.
requirements: lookup must be the lookup object provided to the CRL lookup callback invocation.
Intended to be called from within the CRL lookup callback; for asynchronous flows, it may be called after the callback returns to unblock s2n_negotiate().
Returns S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure.

functions.name: s2n_config_set_cert_validation_cb
functions.signature: int s2n_config_set_cert_validation_cb(struct s2n_config *config, s2n_cert_validation_callback callback, void *context)
functions.description: Registers a callback for performing additional, application-defined validation of the peer’s certificate chain after s2n-tls’s built-in validation. The callback may be used synchronously or asynchronously.
requirements: config must point to a valid s2n_config.
callback will be invoked after receiving and validating the peer’s certificate chain.
Within the callback, applications can retrieve the peer’s cert chain via s2n_connection_get_peer_cert_chain() or s2n_connection_get_client_cert_chain().
For synchronous validation, the callback must call s2n_cert_validation_accept() on success or s2n_cert_validation_reject() on failure before returning.

For asynchronous validation, the callback may return S2N_SUCCESS without calling accept/reject; this pauses the handshake and s2n_negotiate() will indicate S2N_BLOCKED_ON_APPLICATION_INPUT until one of accept/reject is called.
context is an optional application pointer passed through to the callback.

functions.name: s2n_cert_validation_accept
functions.signature: int s2n_cert_validation_accept(struct s2n_cert_validation_info *info)
functions.description: Signals that application-defined certificate validation performed via the cert validation callback succeeded, allowing the handshake to continue.
requirements: info must be the cert validation info object associated with the current callback/connection; it shares the same lifetime as the s2n_connection.
Must be called to continue the handshake if the application’s validation is successful in the synchronous path; for asynchronous use, call to unpause a previously blocked handshake.
Returns S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure.

functions.name: s2n_cert_validation_reject
functions.signature: int s2n_cert_validation_reject(struct s2n_cert_validation_info *info)
functions.description: Signals that application-defined certificate validation failed, causing s2n_negotiate() to error with a protocol error indicating certificate rejection.
requirements: info must be the cert validation info object associated with the current callback/connection; it shares the same lifetime as the s2n_connection.
Must be called to indicate failure in the synchronous path; for asynchronous use, call to unpause a previously blocked handshake with failure.
Returns S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure.

functions.name: s2n_config_add_custom_x509_extension
functions.signature: int s2n_config_add_custom_x509_extension(struct s2n_config *config, uint8_t *extension_oid, uint32_t extension_oid_len);
functions.description: Registers a custom critical X.509 extension OID on an s2n_config so that s2n-tls will ignore that extension during certificate validation. This allows applications to handle validation of those critical extensions themselves (for example in the s2n_cert_validation_callback) or immediately after the handshake and before any application data is sent or accepted. Adds a single extension per call; call multiple times to register multiple OIDs. Available when s2n-tls is built with AWS-LC >= 1.51.0.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized pointer to an s2n_config to be updated (inferred from parameter type and naming).
extension_oid must point to the bytes of the extension OID to register; extension_oid_len specifies its length in bytes (inferred from parameter names and comments).

Callers must implement validation for all registered custom critical extensions outside of s2n-tls, either in the s2n_cert_validation_callback or immediately after the handshake and before any application data is sent or accepted (explicit).
To affect certificate validation for a connection, the extension must be registered on the s2n_config used by that connection before the handshake begins (inferred from purpose).
Adds one extension per call; invoke multiple times to add multiple OIDs (explicit).
Function returns S2N_SUCCESS on success and S2N_FAILURE on failure; callers must check the return value (explicit).
Feature requires s2n-tls built against AWS-LC >= 1.51.0 (explicit environment/build requirement).

functions.name: s2n_config_set_subscriber
functions.signature: int s2n_config_set_subscriber(struct s2n_config *config, void *subscriber);
functions.description: Associates an opaque subscriber pointer with the given s2n_config. This subscriber is later passed to event callbacks (for example, to s2n_event_on_handshake_cb) so the application can correlate events to its own context. Typical usage is to call this during configuration setup before enabling or starting any handshakes. Return value/error semantics are not documented here.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized struct s2n_config pointer.
subscriber is an application-provided opaque pointer; its lifetime should extend at least through any period in which callbacks may be invoked (inferred from common callback patterns).
Return value semantics are unknown; callers should consult s2n documentation for success/failure conventions.

functions.name: s2n_config_set_handshake_event
functions.signature: int s2n_config_set_handshake_event(struct s2n_config *config, s2n_event_on_handshake_cb callback);
functions.description: Registers a callback to receive a handshake event for connections using the provided s2n_config. The callback is invoked with the connection, the subscriber pointer (set via s2n_config_set_subscriber), and a pointer to a transient s2n_event_handshake structure describing the negotiated protocol, cipher, group, and timing information. No event is emitted if the handshake fails. The event structure is only valid for the duration of the callback and must not be accessed after the callback returns. Return value/error semantics are not documented here.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized struct s2n_config pointer.
callback must be a valid function pointer of type s2n_event_on_handshake_cb: void (*)(struct s2n_connection *conn, void *subscriber, struct s2n_event_handshake *event).
The s2n_event_handshake *event provided to the callback is only valid during the callback’s execution and must not be referenced after the callback returns (explicitly stated).
No handshake event will be emitted if the handshake fails (explicitly stated).

If the application relies on the subscriber argument in the callback, it should have been set earlier via s2n_config_set_subscriber and must remain valid for the lifetime of potential callbacks (inferred from API pattern).
Return value semantics are unknown; callers should consult s2n documentation for success/failure conventions.

functions.name: s2n_fingerprint_new
functions.signature: S2N_API struct s2n_fingerprint *s2n_fingerprint_new(s2n_fingerprint_type type);
functions.description: Allocates and returns a reusable s2n_fingerprint context configured for the specified fingerprinting algorithm (e.g., JA3, JA4). Intended to be reused across multiple ClientHello fingerprinting operations to minimize allocations. The returned context must be paired with s2n_fingerprint_free when no longer needed.
requirements: type must be a valid s2n_fingerprint_type value (e.g., S2N_FINGERPRINT_JA3, S2N_FINGERPRINT_JA4)
The returned pointer must be freed with s2n_fingerprint_free
unknown: thread-safety and allocation failure conditions are not specified

functions.name: s2n_fingerprint_free
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_fingerprint_free(struct s2n_fingerprint **fingerprint);
functions.description: Frees memory allocated by s2n_fingerprint_new and invalidates the caller’s pointer.
requirements: fingerprint must be non-null and point to a pointer obtained from s2n_fingerprint_new
The pointed-to s2n_fingerprint must not be used after a successful free
Returns S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure

functions.name: s2n_fingerprint_wipe
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_fingerprint_wipe(struct s2n_fingerprint *fingerprint);
functions.description: Resets an existing s2n_fingerprint context so it can be safely reused with a different ClientHello.
requirements: fingerprint must be a valid s2n_fingerprint previously created by s2n_fingerprint_new
Returns S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure

functions.name: s2n_fingerprint_set_client_hello
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_fingerprint_set_client_hello(struct s2n_fingerprint *fingerprint, struct s2n_client_hello *ch);
functions.description: Sets the ClientHello that the fingerprint context will operate on. The ClientHello is not copied and must outlive the fingerprinting operation.
requirements: fingerprint must be a valid s2n_fingerprint created by s2n_fingerprint_new
ch must remain valid for at least the duration of the fingerprinting call(s) that use it (it is not copied)
Returns S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure

functions.name: s2n_fingerprint_get_hash_size
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_fingerprint_get_hash_size(const struct s2n_fingerprint *fingerprint, uint32_t *size);
functions.description: Retrieves the fixed size of the fingerprint hash for the configured algorithm (size depends on the algorithm but is constant per algorithm).
requirements: fingerprint must be a valid s2n_fingerprint created by s2n_fingerprint_new
size must be non-null and writable
Returns S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure

functions.name: s2n_fingerprint_get_hash
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_fingerprint_get_hash(struct s2n_fingerprint *fingerprint, uint32_t max_output_size, uint8_t *output, uint32_t *output_size);
functions.description: Computes the fingerprint hash for the currently set ClientHello using the context’s algorithm and writes it to output. For JA3 this is a hex-encoded MD5 string; for JA4 it is a composite string with truncated SHA256 components.
requirements: fingerprint must be a valid s2n_fingerprint created by s2n_fingerprint_new
A ClientHello must have been set via s2n_fingerprint_set_client_hello before calling
output must be non-null and have capacity of at least max_output_size bytes
output_size must be non-null
max_output_size must be large enough for the algorithm’s output; otherwise an S2N_ERR_T_USAGE error occurs (use s2n_fingerprint_get_hash_size to size the buffer)
Returns S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure

functions.name: s2n_fingerprint_get_raw_size
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_fingerprint_get_raw_size(const struct s2n_fingerprint *fingerprint, uint32_t *size);
functions.description: Returns the size of the raw fingerprint string most recently computed for this context. Because the raw size depends on the ClientHello, it is only known after computing the fingerprint.
requirements: fingerprint must be a valid s2n_fingerprint created by s2n_fingerprint_new
size must be non-null and writable
Either s2n_fingerprint_get_hash or s2n_fingerprint_get_raw must have been called prior to this call; otherwise the size is not known
Returns S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure

functions.name: s2n_fingerprint_get_raw
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_fingerprint_get_raw(struct s2n_fingerprint *fingerprint, uint32_t max_output_size, uint8_t *output, uint32_t *output_size);
functions.description: Computes the raw fingerprint string for the currently set ClientHello (format depends on algorithm: JA3 lists of decimal values; JA4 prefix and lists of hex values) and writes it to output.
requirements: fingerprint must be a valid s2n_fingerprint created by s2n_fingerprint_new
A ClientHello must have been set via s2n_fingerprint_set_client_hello before calling
output must be non-null and have capacity of at least max_output_size bytes
output_size must be non-null
max_output_size must be large enough; otherwise an S2N_ERR_T_USAGE error occurs
After a successful call, s2n_fingerprint_get_raw_size can be used to retrieve the size of the last raw string
Returns S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure

functions.name: s2n_client_hello_get_fingerprint_hash
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_client_hello_get_fingerprint_hash(struct s2n_client_hello *ch, s2n_fingerprint_type type, uint32_t max_hash_size, uint8_t *hash, uint32_t *hash_size, uint32_t *str_size);
functions.description: One-shot helper that computes the fingerprint hash for the given ClientHello without creating a reusable context. Currently only S2N_FINGERPRINT_JA3 is supported; the output is a hex-encoded MD5 of the raw string. Also returns the size of the full raw string via str_size to help size buffers for the string variant.
requirements: ch must be a valid struct s2n_client_hello pointer
type must currently be S2N_FINGERPRINT_JA3; other values are not supported per documentation
hash and hash_size must be non-null
str_size must be non-null to receive the associated raw string size
max_hash_size must be at least the required hash size (currently at least 16 bytes for JA3); otherwise an S2N_ERR_T_USAGE error occurs
Returns S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure

functions.name: s2n_client_hello_get_fingerprint_string
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_client_hello_get_fingerprint_string(struct s2n_client_hello *ch, s2n_fingerprint_type type, uint32_t max_size, uint8_t *output, uint32_t *output_size);
functions.description: One-shot helper that computes the full, variable-length fingerprint string for the given ClientHello. Because the length is unknown until computed, callers can first use s2n_client_hello_get_fingerprint_hash to obtain the required size via str_size.
requirements: ch must be a valid struct s2n_client_hello pointer
type must currently be S2N_FINGERPRINT_JA3; other values are not supported per documentation
output and output_size must be non-null
max_size must be sufficient for the resulting string; otherwise an S2N_ERR_T_USAGE error occurs
Returns S2N_SUCCESS on success, S2N_FAILURE on failure

functions.name: s2n_connection_ktls_enable_send
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_connection_ktls_enable_send(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Enable kernel TLS (kTLS) for sending on the given s2n-tls connection. After success, s2n_send, s2n_sendv, and s2n_sendv_with_offset use kTLS; s2n_sendfile becomes available. Intended to be called after the TLS handshake completes and before the handshake state is freed. kTLS support is limited and platform-dependent; if enabling fails, the connection can continue without kTLS.
requirements: Must be running on Linux with a kernel that supports kTLS (Linux > 4.13 recommended).
The TLS kernel module must be enabled/loaded (e.g., modprobe tls).
The connection must negotiate AES128-GCM or AES256-GCM ciphers.
Must not use the unstable renegotiation callback (s2n_renegotiate_request_cb); the kernel TLS module does not support renegotiation.
By default, the connection must negotiate TLS 1.2. For TLS 1.3, s2n_config_ktls_enable_unsafe_tls13 must be called beforehand and its caveats apply.
Must not use s2n_connection_set_recv_buffering when using kTLS.
Call only after the handshake completes and before freeing the handshake with s2n_connection_free_handshake.
There must be no pending application data that requires flushing when this is called.
conn must be a valid, initialized s2n_connection pointer.
Caller should handle return value: S2N_SUCCESS on success; S2N_FAILURE if kTLS not enabled (connection may proceed without kTLS).

functions.name: s2n_connection_ktls_enable_recv
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_connection_ktls_enable_recv(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Enable kernel TLS (kTLS) for receiving on the given s2n-tls connection. After success, s2n_recv uses kTLS. Intended to be called after the TLS handshake completes and before the handshake state is freed. kTLS support is limited and platform-dependent; if enabling fails, the connection can continue without kTLS.
requirements: Must be running on Linux with a kernel that supports kTLS (Linux > 4.13 recommended).
The TLS kernel module must be enabled/loaded (e.g., modprobe tls).
The connection must negotiate AES128-GCM or AES256-GCM ciphers.
Must not use the unstable renegotiation callback (s2n_renegotiate_request_cb); the kernel TLS module does not support renegotiation.
By default, the connection must negotiate TLS 1.2. For TLS 1.3, s2n_config_ktls_enable_unsafe_tls13 must be called beforehand and its caveats apply.
Must not use s2n_connection_set_recv_buffering when using kTLS.
Call only after the handshake completes and before freeing the handshake with s2n_connection_free_handshake.
There must be no buffered application data that requires draining when this is called.
conn must be a valid, initialized s2n_connection pointer.
Caller should handle return value: S2N_SUCCESS on success; S2N_FAILURE if kTLS not enabled (connection may proceed without kTLS).

functions.name: s2n_config_ktls_enable_unsafe_tls13
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_config_ktls_enable_unsafe_tls13(struct s2n_config *config);
functions.description: Allow kTLS to be enabled for connections that negotiate TLS 1.3. Marked “unsafe” because only Linux kernels >= 6.14 support TLS 1.3 key updates in kTLS, and s2n-tls cannot detect kernel support; key updates without the patch will cause connection failure. Also enforces a 388GB per-call limit on s2n_send and s2n_sendfile.
requirements: Must be called before enabling kTLS on a connection via s2n_connection_ktls_enable_send or s2n_connection_ktls_enable_recv.
On kernels without TLS 1.3 key update support (Linux < 6.14), receiving or sending a TLS 1.3 key update will cause a connection failure; callers accept this risk when enabling.
After calling this API, do not call s2n_send or s2n_sendfile with a size/count parameter exceeding 388GB; S2N_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT will be raised if the limit is exceeded.
config must be a valid, initialized s2n_config pointer.
Caller should handle return value: S2N_SUCCESS on success; S2N_FAILURE otherwise.

functions.name: s2n_connection_get_key_update_counts
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_connection_get_key_update_counts(struct s2n_connection *conn, uint8_t *send_key_updates, uint8_t *recv_key_updates);
functions.description: Report how many times the sending and receiving traffic keys have been updated on a TLS 1.3 connection. s2n-tls counts are capped at UINT8_MAX (255); a value of 255 indicates 255 or more updates.
requirements: Applies only to TLS 1.3; earlier protocol versions do not support key updates.
conn must be a valid, initialized s2n_connection pointer.
send_key_updates must be a non-NULL, writable pointer to at least one byte to receive the send update count.
recv_key_updates must be a non-NULL, writable pointer to at least one byte to receive the recv update count.
Caller should handle return value: S2N_SUCCESS on success; S2N_FAILURE otherwise.
Reported counts saturate at 255; actual updates may exceed this value.

functions.name: s2n_sendfile
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_sendfile(struct s2n_connection *conn, int fd, off_t offset, size_t count, size_t *bytes_written, s2n_blocked_status *blocked);
functions.description: Send file contents as TLS application data using kTLS send-path for improved efficiency (kernel-side copy). Available only when kTLS is enabled for sending on the connection. bytes_written returns the number of bytes written; blocked reports the blocked status on S2N_ERR_T_BLOCKED.
requirements: kTLS must be enabled for sending on the connection (via s2n_connection_ktls_enable_send).
fd must be opened for reading and support mmap-like operations; it must not be a socket.
For TLS 1.3 connections, the count argument is used to enforce safe sending limits; applications should not set count excessively high.
conn must be a valid, initialized s2n_connection pointer.
bytes_written must be a non-NULL, writable pointer to receive the number of bytes written on success.
blocked must be a non-NULL, writable pointer to receive the blocked status if S2N_ERR_T_BLOCKED is returned.
Caller should handle return value: S2N_SUCCESS if any bytes are written; S2N_FAILURE otherwise.

functions.name: s2n_config_set_npn
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_config_set_npn(struct s2n_config *config, bool enable);
functions.description: Enable or disable support for the TLS Next Protocol Negotiation (NPN) extension on an s2n-tls configuration. When enabled, s2n-tls clients will send the NPN extension and servers will respond if the peer supports NPN; if ALPN is also indicated by the peer, ALPN is preferred. Use s2n_config_append_protocol_preference() to set the list of supported protocols, and after handshake completion retrieve the negotiated protocol via s2n_get_application_protocol(). NPN is not recommended and is supported for interoperability (draft-agl-tls-nextprotoneg-03, e.g., with OpenSSL).
requirements: config must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid s2n_config object (typically created via s2n_config_new).
enable must be a boolean value: true to enable NPN, false to disable.
Callers must check the return value: S2N_SUCCESS (0) on success, S2N_FAILURE (-1) on error.
If specific protocol preferences are desired for NPN negotiation, they must be configured separately via s2n_config_append_protocol_preference().
Behavior when called relative to connection creation/handshake timing is not specified in this header; typically this should be configured on the s2n_config before it is used to create connections.

functions.name: s2n_config_set_renegotiate_request_cb
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_config_set_renegotiate_request_cb(struct s2n_config *config, s2n_renegotiate_request_cb callback, void *context);
functions.description: Registers a callback that s2n-tls will invoke when a client receives a server request to renegotiate the TLS 1.2 (or earlier) connection. The callback can be invoked multiple times if multiple requests are received. Use the callback’s response out-parameter to indicate whether to ignore, reject, or accept and proceed with renegotiation. Typical usage: configure once on the s2n_config before creating or using client connections that may need renegotiation.
requirements: config must point to a valid, initialized s2n_config instance.
callback must be a function matching s2n_renegotiate_request_cb (struct s2n_connection*, void*, s2n_renegotiate_response*).
The callback may be called multiple times by s2n-tls if multiple renegotiation requests are received.
Callers must check the return value and handle S2N_SUCCESS or S2N_FAILURE accordingly.
Behavior is intended for clients; servers do not perform renegotiation (callback may not be used on servers).
Acceptance of a NULL callback to clear the handler is unknown (not specified in the provided header).

functions.name: s2n_renegotiate_wipe
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_renegotiate_wipe(struct s2n_connection *conn);
functions.description: Prepares an existing client connection for renegotiation by wiping most connection state while preserving enough to continue encrypting/decrypting records with the old keys. This must be called before s2n_renegotiate. After wiping, the application must re-apply any connection-specific configuration it previously set, except file descriptors and send/recv callbacks which are preserved.
requirements: Must be called before s2n_renegotiate.
The connection must be a client connection; calling on a server connection will fail.

All in-progress I/O must be completed before calling: the last call to s2n_send must have succeeded, s2n_peek must return zero, and there must be no data in the send or receive buffers; otherwise this call will fail.
Must not be called from inside s2n_renegotiate_request_cb (the receive call that triggered the callback must complete first).
Will fail if the connection has indicated it will be serialized via s2n_config_set_serialization_version().

After this call, the application must repeat any connection-specific setup it performed previously (for example, s2n_connection_set_blinding), except: file descriptors (set via s2n_connection_set_fd/read_fd/write_fd) and the send/recv callbacks (and their ctx) are preserved.
Callers must check the return value and handle S2N_SUCCESS or S2N_FAILURE accordingly.
conn must be a valid, initialized s2n_connection pointer.

functions.name: s2n_renegotiate
functions.signature: S2N_API int s2n_renegotiate(struct s2n_connection *conn, uint8_t *app_data_buf, ssize_t app_data_buf_size, ssize_t *app_data_size, s2n_blocked_status *blocked);
functions.description: Performs a renegotiation handshake on an already established client connection, with return/blocked behavior like s2n_negotiate. Unlike initial handshake, this may encounter valid application data; in that case it returns S2N_FAILURE with error type S2N_ERR_T_BLOCKED, sets blocked to S2N_BLOCKED_ON_APPLICATION_DATA, copies the data into app_data_buf, and sets app_data_size. The application should process that data and then call s2n_renegotiate again until the handshake completes.
requirements: s2n_renegotiate_wipe must have been called on conn before calling this function.
The connection must be a client connection; calling on a server connection will fail.
Must not be called from inside s2n_renegotiate_request_cb. The receive call that triggered the callback must complete before calling this function (or s2n_renegotiate_wipe).
app_data_buf must point to writable memory of at least app_data_buf_size bytes.
app_data_size must be a valid pointer to receive the number of bytes of application data copied.
blocked must be a valid pointer that will be set to the current blocked status, including S2N_BLOCKED_ON_APPLICATION_DATA when applicable.
Behavior and handling of blocked statuses should mirror s2n_negotiate; callers must loop/retry as indicated by blocked status and error types.
Callers must check the return value: S2N_SUCCESS if the handshake completed; S2N_FAILURE if an error occurred or operation is blocked.
